_note: Authored metric dictionary. Coverage numbers are NOT stored here - they are read at runtime from BUILD.json, which is generated from the source, so what a user sees can never drift from the data. Every threshold carries verified_by; a threshold without a source does not ship.

lead_level_mg_l.label: Lead level
lead_level_mg_l.definition: Lead concentration reported for the drinking-water system mapped to this ZIP code, as published in the source dataset.
lead_level_mg_l.upstream: EPA SDWIS and utility Consumer Confidence Reports

threshold.name: EPA lead action level
threshold.note: 15 ppb. Exceeding it in more than 10% of sampled customer taps triggers corrosion-control obligations for the system. The 2024 Lead and Copper Rule Improvements phase in further requirements; confirm the currently applicable value with the system before relying on it.

lead_level_mg_l.what_missing_means: No lead figure is published for this ZIP in the snapshot. It is not a result of zero and not evidence that the water was tested.
caveats: A reported value of exactly 0 appears for thousands of ZIP codes. A laboratory cannot report a true zero; treat 0 as 'below the detection limit', not as 'no lead present'.
This is a system-level figure. Lead most often enters water from the service line and household plumbing, so an individual home can differ sharply from its system.
The aggregation method and monitoring period behind this number are not documented in the open dataset. Only the snapshot publication date is known, which is not a sampling date.

aggregation.note: The open dataset does not state how this figure is aggregated or which monitoring period it covers. Do not describe it as a 90th percentile, a mean, or a current result.
aggregation.evidence: Measured 2026-08-30: the companion CCR records carry a SEPARATE lead_90th_percentile field, and it disagrees with this one. Across 14 systems that publish both, only 1 matched under either unit reading. So this value is demonstrably not simply the CCR 90th percentile.
aggregation.why_we_do_not_use_the_other_field: lead_90th_percentile is internally inconsistent in units across records (neighbouring systems report 0.002, 1.2 and 7 for the same quantity), so it is not read by this project at all.

copper_action_level_exceedance.label: Copper action level exceedance
copper_action_level_exceedance.definition: Whether the system exceeded the EPA copper action level.
copper_action_level_exceedance.what_missing_means: The source records only positive exceedances. A blank therefore distinguishes neither 'no exceedance' nor 'never tested', and must not be rendered as false.
caveats: Only 3.1% of rows carry a value, and the only value ever present is true.

radon_zone.label: EPA radon zone
radon_zone.definition: EPA Map of Radon Zones classification for the county: 1 is the highest predicted indoor screening level, 3 the lowest.

threshold.name: EPA radon action level
threshold.citation: EPA recommended action level for indoor radon
threshold.note: Zone 1 counties have a predicted average indoor screening level above 4 pCi/L.

radon_zone.what_missing_means: No zone is published for this ZIP.
caveats: A zone is a county-level prediction, not a measurement of any building. EPA recommends testing every home regardless of zone; a zone 3 home can still measure high.

total_violations.label: Drinking-water violations
total_violations.definition: Count of recorded drinking-water violations for the system serving this ZIP.
total_violations.what_missing_means: No violation record was matched to this ZIP. That is a gap in matching or reporting, not a finding of compliance.
caveats: Includes monitoring and reporting violations, which are procedural, alongside health-based ones. Use health_violations for the health-relevant subset.
Counts records matched to this ZIP, not events. A zero can equally mean nothing happened, nothing was reported, or nothing was matched.

health_violations.label: Health-based violations
health_violations.definition: Violations of a health-based standard, as distinct from monitoring or reporting failures.
health_violations.what_missing_means: No health-based violation record was matched to this ZIP. Not a finding that the water met every standard.
caveats: A ZIP is not a water system. The dataset maps each ZIP to one public water system, but ZIP and service-area boundaries do not nest. For example the dataset assigns 90210 to the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power, while the City of Beverly Hills operates its own system for much of that area. Verify the provider for a specific address before acting.

unresolved_violations.label: Unresolved violations
unresolved_violations.definition: Violations recorded as still open rather than returned to compliance.
unresolved_violations.what_missing_means: No open-violation record was matched to this ZIP.

enforcement_action_count.label: Enforcement actions
enforcement_action_count.definition: Formal or informal enforcement actions recorded against the system.
enforcement_action_count.what_missing_means: No enforcement record was matched to this ZIP.
caveats: An enforcement action means a regulator responded. Its absence does not mean nothing happened.

enforcement_health_violations.label: Enforcement actions on health violations
enforcement_health_violations.definition: The subset of enforcement actions tied to health-based violations.
enforcement_health_violations.what_missing_means: No such record was matched to this ZIP.

has_active_issues.label: Active issues flag
has_active_issues.definition: Whether the source flags the system as currently having active issues.
has_active_issues.upstream: ZipCheckup, derived from EPA SDWIS status
has_active_issues.what_missing_means: The flag is not set for this ZIP, which is not the same as being set to false.

contaminant_count.label: Contaminants recorded
contaminant_count.definition: Number of distinct contaminants recorded in violation for the system.
contaminant_count.what_missing_means: No contaminant records were matched to this ZIP.
caveats: Counts contaminants that appear in violation records, not everything present in the water.

health_contaminant_names.label: Health-relevant contaminants
health_contaminant_names.definition: Names of contaminants tied to health-based violations.
health_contaminant_names.what_missing_means: No named health contaminant was matched to this ZIP.
caveats: Free text from the upstream record; wording varies between states.

home_safety_score.label: Home safety score

threshold.reason: A vendor composite with no statutory threshold. It is not an EPA metric and no regulation defines a passing value.

home_safety_score.what_missing_means: No score was computed for this ZIP. It is not a score of 0 and not a grade of F.
caveats: The inputs and weights behind the composite are not documented in the open dataset, so the score should not be treated as a measurement.

home_safety_grade.label: Home safety grade
home_safety_grade.definition: Letter grade A-F corresponding to the composite score.

threshold.reason: Derived from the composite score; no statutory basis.

home_safety_grade.what_missing_means: No grade was computed for this ZIP.
caveats: Present exactly when home_safety_score is present.

boil_water_advisories.label: Boil-water advisories
boil_water_advisories.definition: Count of boil-water advisories issued for the system.
boil_water_advisories.what_missing_means: This column exists in the source schema but is empty for every row of the snapshot, so the dataset carries no advisory information at all.
caveats: Shipped deliberately as a permanent unknown: telling an agent the field exists and is empty is safer than omitting it and letting the agent assume none were issued.
